title: Private Cluster Fault-Domain Visual Debugger — status ribbon & upgrade impact preview
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem statement: Operators on Private/VPC deployments need a quick, low-noise way to understand which nodes and fault domains are affected during rolling upgrades, and to preview upgrade impact before kicking off a rollout. Existing cluster status pages show health and recent events but do not make fault-domain relationships explicit or allow simulated 'what-if' upgrade previews.

Goal: Design a compact visual debugger embedded in the Private Cluster Overview that: (1) surfaces per-fault-domain health and capacity; (2) overlays ongoing/upcoming upgrade steps as a timeline ribbon; (3) provides a simulated impact preview when selecting an upgrade plan or a specific node pool; and (4) includes actionable next steps (drain, abort, reschedule) surfaced to operators and engineers.

Scope: Prototype UI components (status ribbon, fault-domain map, upgrade preview modal), interaction patterns for simulation, review-ready annotations for engineering handoff. Not in scope: implementation of the simulation engine (ENG), integration with RBAC (separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Status ribbon shows each fault-domain as a chip with aggregated health (healthy/warn/error) and capacity indicators
Hovering a chip calls out nodes in that domain and recent failures (last 24h) in a contextual flyout
Upgrade timeline ribbon visualizes planned vs in-flight steps and can be scrubbed to preview state at each step
Preview modal runs a deterministic, read-only simulation (client-side mock) that shows which pods/tenants would be moved, expected latency increase, and estimated extra cost for the window
All interactions have keyboard access and meet AA accessibility for contrast and focus order
Design deliverables include Figma frames, tokenized CSS guidance, and a short spec for events/telemetry required by ENG
design_notes: Prefer a horizontal status ribbon above the cluster topology to conserve vertical space in the Console
Use color semantics consistent with Console (green/amber/crimson) but add a pattern texture for users with colorblindness
Fault-domain map should default to compressed 'lane' view and allow expansion into a node-grid with per-node hover affordances
Preview modal must be read-only and clearly labeled as 'simulation' with toggles for aggression level (conservative/standard/aggressive) to reflect different drain policies
Expose a lightweight JSON export of the simulation summary to attach to runbooks/incidents
decisions: Show fault-domain chips in ribbon rather than a full map by default to keep Overview page scannable
Include an 'Impact score' (0-100) in the preview to quickly indicate blast radius — computed by ENG but surfaced here as a single metric
Do not allow the preview to start a rollout — simulation button launches modal only; actual 'Start rollout' is a separate CTA guarded by RBAC
For initial rollout, default to conservative simulation to avoid surprising operators; include explicit 'simulate aggressive' checkbox
open_questions: ENG: Can runtime produce the node-level metrics needed for a meaningful simulation (drain time, live connections, tenant weight)? (see ENG-48212)
PM: Should the preview surface estimated cost in dollars or in % increase relative to baseline? Customers asked for both in interviews.
Security: Does exporting simulation JSON need additional audit logging or redaction for tenant IDs?
DX: Where should we store user preferences for ribbon density (compact vs expanded) across clusters?
